gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Notebookcheck measured the Lenovo Idea Tab Pro, ChatGPT's 'best budget large screen' pick, at only 409 nits maximum brightness. On the same Notebookcheck rig the cheaper Galaxy Tab S10 FE reached 667 nits and also ran longest in the Wi-Fi web-surfing test (14 h 47 min, against the Idea Tab Pro's 13 h 18 min).
standout_why: The only rival page I could read in full was mynexttablet.com/best-tablets-keyboards (cited). It gives in-house battery hours (S10 FE 8.5 h, S11 12.75 h, S11 Ultra 14.2 h) and maker-claimed brightness ('up to 800 nits' for the S10 FE), and it leaves out the Lenovo Idea Tab Pro completely. It has no measured brightness and no measured weight with a keyboard. Tech Advisor (article 723363) gives runtimes only for the Redmi Pad 2 and Galaxy Tab A11, and its only Lenovo is the non-Pro Idea Tab. wired.com returned 'unable to fetch', androidauthority.com returned 403, and tomsguide.com came back truncated, so I could not check those three. Notebookcheck's runtimes also contradict MyNextTablet's ranking: Notebookcheck has the S10 FE outlasting the S11 and the S11 Ultra, while MyNextTablet puts the S10 FE last of the three.
decides: It supports the Galaxy Tab S10 FE as the value pick: it was the brightest of the two budget tablets and ran longest in Wi-Fi browsing. It weakens the Idea Tab Pro: buyers who work near windows or outdoors should know it measured about 400 nits, and the newer Idea Tab Pro Gen 2 measured 618 nits and 14 h 11 min. It also tempers the S11 Ultra as the 'laptop alternative'. Its Wi-Fi runtime (13 h 9 min) was shorter than the S10 FE's, and Notebookcheck rated its keyboard 71/80.
